# Investor privacy notice

*Version 2026-10-23-draft-2. Status: draft.*

## Who we are

Anker AI [legal form and registered office in Berlin, Germany] runs Anker. Contact for anything about your data: privacy@an-ker.de [and the data-protection officer, if one is appointed]. We run Anker, a platform for venture funds, founders and investors. For your investor account we decide how and why your data is used (we are the controller).

## What this notice covers

Your investor account on Anker: finding funds, asking funds to talk, conversations with funds, your investor documents (if available), and being found by funds if you choose.

## What we collect, and why

- Your account: email address, name, password (kept by our sign-in provider as a hash) and when you accepted the terms. To give you an account (contract).

- Your profile and entities: name, country, languages, how you want to be contacted, a short description; for each entity you invest through: its name, kind, country, tax residence, the category of investor you say you are, and what you look for. To show you funds that fit and to let you ask them to talk (contract; steps at your request).

- Requests and conversations: the requests you send and what you chose to share, the messages and files you exchange with a fund, NDAs you accept (a copy of the text, the time, your IP address and a hash of your browser details, as evidence), meetings you arrange. To carry out what you asked for (steps at your request); the NDA record to keep evidence (legitimate interest).

- Identity documents (optional, when available): copies you add to your passport, and a record of which fund received a copy and when. Only if you add them, and shared only when you choose (consent).

- Being found (optional, off by default): if you switch it on, funds that fit see a card without your name, email or team. We record when you switched it on and which wording you saw (consent).

- Security and abuse prevention: sign-up attempts and limits, and a log of who did what on your entity (legitimate interest).

## Who receives it

A fund receives only what you choose to share when you ask to talk or accept its invitation, your email address when it accepts, and documents only when you share them. Our service providers process data for us: hosting, database, sign-in and email delivery (the current list is on the sub-processors page). We do not send your investor data to AI providers.

## Where

Our database is hosted in the United States (AWS us-east-1, through Neon). [Regions of sign-in and email delivery, and the safeguards for transfers outside the EU, to be completed once confirmed.]

## How long we keep it

- A pending sign-up (address, name, hashed code): 1 day after it was asked for. Then: deleted.

- A pending code to link a record a fund added: 1 day. Then: deleted.

- Answered, revoked and expired team invitations (an email address): 30 days after they closed. Then: deleted.

- A fund's discoverability invitation nobody answered: 30 days. Then: closed as withdrawn.

- The card a fund saw, kept on an answered invitation: 180 days after the answer. Then: the card is emptied; the fact and date of the invitation stay (they enforce the 90-day wait after a decline).

- Identity documents in the passport of an entity that was archived: 30 days after archiving. Then: file contents wiped.

- A replaced passport record that was never shared: 30 days. Then: deleted (the bytes were wiped when it was replaced).

- Files attached to messages in a conversation that ended (declined or withdrawn): 365 days after it ended. Then: files deleted; the messages stay.

- The entity's activity log (who did what): 1095 days (three years). Then: deleted.

- Your account and the data in it: until you delete them.

- Funds you have dealt with keep their own records, with your name removed if you erase your account, and anything they have already checked in their onboarding, under their own retention.

## Your rights

Access and a copy (Download my data on your profile), correction (edit your profile), erasure (Delete my investor account), withdrawal of consent (switch off being found; take back a shared document), restriction and objection (write to privacy@an-ker.de), and complaint to your supervisory authority; if you live in Germany, or if our seat is in Berlin, that is the Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information, or the authority of the state where you live. [Counsel to confirm.]

## Funds are separate controllers

Once you ask a fund to talk, the fund also holds the information you gave it and is responsible for it under its own privacy notice. Ask the fund to correct or delete what it holds.

## Automated decisions

We rank funds by how well their stated focus matches what you say you look for. This is not advice and not a recommendation, and it is not a decision with legal or similar effect.

## Changes

If we change this notice in a way that matters, we will tell you by email or in the app and, if the change affects your terms, ask you to accept the new version.
